## The three Rs on one claim {#the-three-rs-on-one-claim}

:::: {.none}
::: {.fragment}
**Reproduction**: three of five analyses came back to the third decimal, once the data, the code and the right version of a public series were in hand.
:::

::: {.fragment}
**Robustness**: five careful analysts asked five different questions of the same claim, and their answers differ several times over.
:::

::: {.fragment}
**Replication**: on new waves the sign of the claim did not hold, and a preregistration is how the next attempt fixes its plan before it knows the result.
:::
::::

::: notes
Three sentences to close the day, one for each R. Reproduction: you brought back three of the five analyses to the third decimal, and it took more than code and data. It took the right version of a public series and a careful reading of what each analyst actually did, slips included. [advance] Robustness: five competent analysts, given the same claim and the same instructions, asked five different questions of it, and their answers differ several times over. We looked at that this morning through the estimand. [advance] Replication: on later waves the sign of the claim did not hold. What would make the next attempt more informative is what you wrote in the last hour, a plan fixed before anyone knows the answer.
:::

## What you take with you {.smaller}

::: {.small}
- A reproduction of one of the five reanalyses, to the third decimal, and the slip that its code carries
- An estimand statement for the claim, written by you
- A preregistration for a replication of that analysis, written before any new data were opened
- For reading: the three *Nature* papers of 2026 [@MiskeEtAl2026InvestigatingReproducibilitySocial; @AczelEtAl2026InvestigatingAnalyticalRobustness; @TynerEtAl2026InvestigatingReplicabilitySocial], the glossary of @NosekEtAl2025BriefGlossaryTerms, @LundbergEtAl2021WhatYourEstimand, and the case study on the course site
- For the next step: the companion modules on repositories, on data sources and on Git and GitHub
:::
